stem.text: Water is added to a storage tank at the rate \( r(t) = 12 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} + 15 \) gallons per hour, and removed at the constant rate of 9 gallons per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 8 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 40 gallons of water in the tank, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 8 \) at which the amount A(t) of water is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 8, where A is 88 gallons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 8.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 40 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(12 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{4} \right)} + 6\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = r(t) - 9 = 12 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} + 6 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 2.667 \) and \( t = 5.333 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 40 \), \( A(2.667) \approx 69.232 \), \( A(5.333) \approx 58.768 \), and \( A(8) = 40 + \int_{0}^{8} A'(s)\,ds = 88 \).
The largest candidate value is 88, at the endpoint, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 8 \) hours.

options.label: The amount is greatest at t = 2.667, where A is 69.232 gallons, the larger of the values of A at the two critical points.
options.derivation: the candidates test run on the two critical points only, leaving out both endpoints
